subject: Governing law / injunctive relief carve — HelixPay MSA & Order Form
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie@helixpay.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: legal@helixpay.com
Date: Thu, 03 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixPay redlines — governing law & injunctive relief

Tessa —

Thanks for sending the MSA and Order Form. Our outside counsel reviewed and flagged two items that will be a deal-breaker for our GC unless we can reach a compromise: choice of law and a forum carve for emergency equitable relief.

Chief asks:
- Governing law: they prefer California law (HelixPay HQ) rather than Delaware.
- Injunctive relief: they want the right to seek emergency injunctive relief in California courts without triggering a waiver of arbitration or other forum-selection clauses.

I attached our redlines (Helix_MSA_redlines_v2.docx). Can Redwood accept either California law or a clear, narrowly tailored carve that lets HelixPay seek temporary/provisional injunctive relief in CA while preserving arbitration for merits? If possible, please propose language.

We'd like to get this buttoned up before legal ops issues the PO.

Best,
Ellie Park
Head of Legal Operations
HelixPay, Inc.
Attachment: Helix_MSA_redlines_v2.docx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HelixPay redlines — governing law & injunctive relief

Kimberly / Rishi / Neha —

FYI, Helix's counsel pushed back on Delaware + wants explicit injunctive relief carve to allow emergency relief in CA. They attached redlines.

My read: Helix is firm on California preference only to the extent they can preserve immediate injunctive relief in their home courts. They seem willing to accept our arbitration/venue structure if we add a narrowly tailored carve for interim relief.

Proposal (draft language) — put this in the MSA under Dispute Resolution as an exception to the forum/arbitration selection:

"Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional, injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect the party's confidential information or intellectual property, provided that such request for provisional relief shall not constitute a waiver of, or otherwise prejudice, the obligation of the parties to submit the dispute to arbitration for final determination."

I drafted a short text file with the carve (proposed_injunction_carve.txt) — see attachment.

Questions for legal:
- Is the proposed language sufficient to preserve our arbitration posture and limit forum shopping?
- Any risks around broader waiver or allowing injunctive proceedings in CA that would later block enforcement of arbitration?

If you sign off, I'll send to Helix with a quick note and offer a single inbound/outbound escrow: Delaware law remains for the agreement, but we accept the provisional relief carve for CA.

—Tessa
Attachment: proposed_injunction_carve.txt

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Park <ellie@helixpay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixPay redlines — governing law & injunctive relief

Ellie —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity from your counsel. Our legal team reviewed and we can offer a compromise to avoid a full governing-law swap: Redwood will keep Delaware as the governing law and primary forum/arbitration framework, with a narrowly tailored carve allowing either party to seek provisional or injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (including California) strictly for the purpose of preservation or emergency relief.

Suggested placement: immediately after the arbitration clause, labelled "Interim Equitable Relief". The text we propose is materially the same as the one attached — it explicitly states that seeking such relief will not waive the right to arbitrate the merits.

If Helix agrees, we'll incorporate that carve into the MSA and then lock the Order Form for signature. We'll also note in the PO checklist that Helix has the carve for provisional relief localized to CA if they want to include their state courts for emergency petitions.

Please let me know if Helix counsel wants any additional guardrails (e.g., 7-day notice to Redwood counsel before filing, or scope limitations). Happy to iterate quickly.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships (covering legal coordination)
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Law <michael.law@helixpaylegal.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellie Park <ellie@helixpay.com>, legal@helixpay.com
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: HelixPay redlines — governing law & injunctive relief

Tessa —

Thanks for the fast reply and the draft carve. We reviewed with GC and they find the compromise acceptable in principle. Two small asks before we finalize:

1) Add a short notice provision — Helix will provide Redwood counsel with notice of intent to seek provisional relief, except where immediate ex parte relief is required.
2) Clarify that the carve applies only to provisional or emergency equitable relief and does not permit Helix to litigate merits in state court.

We attached a PDF with our signature redlines (Helix_signature_redlines.pdf). If you can accept the two small edits above, we can move to signature and issue the PO.

Michael Law
Senior Counsel, HelixPay Legal
Attachment: Helix_signature_redlines.pdf
